title: Driver shim tangle debug diary
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad tracking an intermittent GPU OOM / library mismatch that looks like a driver/libcuda shim problem. Notes are noisy — chronological breadcrumbs, commands tried, and hypotheses for a later clean write-up.

Summary of issue:
- Host machines sometimes OOM during model init (large KV cache allocation), but only in certain containers/pods.
- Error surface varies: sometimes CUDA reports an illegal memory access, sometimes the app crashes with dlopen errors about libcuda.so.1, other times nvml init fails in Python with exception "Failed to initialize NVML: unknown error".
- Reproducible on one dev node (gpu-node-17) and sometimes on a cluster worker after a driver upgrade window.

Environment snapshot (mixed):
- Host kernel: 6.1.23-rt (custom)
- Host NVIDIA driver: 525.85.12 (dkms-built module, /proc/driver/nvidia/version shows 525.85.12)
- Container base images observed: nvidia/cuda:11.8-runtime-ubuntu20.04, cuda:12.2-runtime-ubuntu22.04, and smaller slim python images with wheel-installed torch.
- Conda envs + pip wheels for torch compiled against CUDA 11.7/11.8 in many cases.
- Some nodes have both /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (host driver-provided) and container-bundled libcuda in /usr/local/cuda/lib64 (occasionally).

Commands & outputs (snippets taken during repro attempts):
1) Check driver on host:
$ cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version
NVRM version: NVIDIA UNIX x86_64 Kernel Module 525.85.12 Wed Dec 28 10:15:47 UTC 2025

$ nvidia-smi
Thu Mar 12 12:11:04 2026
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+
| NVIDIA-SMI 525.85.12    Driver Version: 525.85.12    CUDA Version: 12.2     |
+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+

2) Inside container (problematic run):
$ python -c "import torch; print(torch.version.cuda); print(torch.cuda.is_available())"
11.8
True

But then run crashes when allocating a 30GB buffer:
RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 31.5 GiB (GPU 0; 80.00 GiB total capacity; 46.3 GiB already allocated; 1.25 GiB free; 2.00 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)

3) Docker inspect and mount situation:
- Container launched with --gpus all and volume mounts: /usr/local/cuda -> host /usr/local/cuda-12.2 (some nodes)
- Other runs use NVIDIA container toolkit enabling host libcuda visibility.

4) ldd of _C.so (torch CUDA extension) inside container:
$ ldd /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so
  libcuda.so.1 => /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 (0x00007f0e...)
  libcudart.so.11.0 => not found
  libcusparse.so.11 => not found
(-> indicates mixed library visibility; loader falls back to host libcuda but missing full cuda toolkit libs)

5) ldconfig cache vs LD_LIBRARY_PATH:
- Container ldconfig shows host-provided libcuda in /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu, but container's /usr/local/cuda/lib64 has cuda 12.2 libs. If LD_LIBRARY_PATH points at /usr/local/cuda/lib64, sometimes the app picks up inconsistent symbols (abi mismatch).

6) Example dlopen error seen in production crashlog:
python: symbol lookup error: /opt/conda/lib/python3.10/site-packages/torch/lib/libc10_cuda.so: undefined symbol: cuGetErrorName
(typical when libcuda provides older/newer symbol set than the runtime expects)

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Shim/mismatched libcuda on loader path: container picks host libcuda by SONAME but other CUDA toolkit libs are from a different version -> symbol mismatch and subtle behavior like malloc not failing properly -> OOMs or illegal accesses.
2) Partial driver upgrade state on some nodes: kernel module updated but userland libs cached in container image layers (docker image built earlier referencing old /usr/local/cuda), causing two versions to be seen at runtime.
3) LD_PRELOAD or site-specific LD_LIBRARY_PATH in launch scripts (we saw /opt/nvidia/lib in one init script) forcing wrong ordering.
4) NVML init sometimes fails because pci device node appears/vanishes during driver module reloads or nvidia-fabric manager restarts; app interprets that as OOM and falls back badly.

Commands I tried to validate hypotheses (notes + results):
- Ran modinfo nvidia on host, compared vermagic vs module in /lib/modules. All matched on node-17.
- Reproduced container with both /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 and /usr/local/cuda/lib64 present and toggled LD_LIBRARY_PATH:
  * With LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64:/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu -> torch crashes with undefined symbol.
  * With LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu:/usr/local/cuda/lib64 -> torch init succeeds but later OOM behavior not consistent.
- ldd tree for Python extension pointed to mixed versions; forcing LD_LIBRARY_PATH to host lib path made symbols resolve but revealed other missing toolkit libs (cusparse, cublas).
- Tried LD_PRELOAD=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> different segfault (illegal instruction) in fast math kernel (likely ABI mismatch).

Interim mitigation tested:
- Added explicit container startup step to run: "update-alternatives --set cuda /usr/local/cuda-12.2" and export LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/usr/local/cuda/lib64 then restart process. This made one failing job succeed (likely because it forced consistent toolkit+runtime).
- For pods that use host mounts for /usr/local/cuda, changed to rely on host drivers only (no container-bundled libcuda) — reduced incidence but not eliminated.

Observations / oddities:
- On some nodes torch reports CUDA 11.x in python even though host nvidia-smi shows CUDA 12.2. That indicates torch was built against 11.x and is finding a compatibility shim.
- Some crash logs show NVML error before memory allocation attempts — suggests driver/userland desync can fail NVML and still allow some CUDA ops, causing inconsistent free memory accounting.
- When the node had ongoing driver updates (post-deploy), restoration via system reboot temporarily fixed the issue for a day.

Next steps (practical plan):
1) Repro script: minimal docker image that purposely contains mismatched libcuda in /usr/local/cuda and host libcuda in /usr/lib, run a short torch program that allocates and frees a bunch of buffers to trigger OOM/illegal access. Goal: produce minimal repro and deterministic crash.
2) Run full binary check: compare SONAMEs and symbol tables (nm -D) of libcuda on host vs container. Capture differences in symbols used by libc10_cuda.so.
3) Coordinate with infra to pin node-17 to a single driver/toolkit stack for testing (either host + container consistent 12.2 or fully rely on host libs and remove container cuda libs).
4) Add container startup validation: run a small script to verify that ldd for critical .so resolves to a consistent directory (all libs from same cuda version). If mismatch, fail fast and emit helpful logs.
5) Add automated check in CI that builds images and runs ldd on torch libs to detect potential multi-version exposure.

Notes / links for later:
- Slack thread: #infra-gpu (referenced messages around Mar 11-12)
- Ticket: JIRA-INF-1872 (driver upgrade window)
- GH: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/789 (runtime container changes)

Random crumbs I wrote while debugging:
- Check /etc/ld.so.conf.d for stale cuda paths that survived image layering.
- If using NVIDIA container toolkit, ensure nvidia-container-runtime-hook isn't injecting old paths.
- Watch for docker build ARGs that bake /usr/local/cuda symlink into image against older host during ephemeral build runner.
- Consider enabling device-level healthcheck in k8s to detect NVML failures and automatically recycle pod.

Conclusion (temporary):
Most evidence points to loader-level mixed-version exposure (host libcuda vs container toolkit libs) producing ABI/behavior inconsistencies. Short-term: add startup ldd checks + enforce single toolkit version in images; long-term: improve infra driver rollout process and add automated ldd-based gating for container images that include CUDA libs.

Timestamped entries:
- 2026-03-10 09:12: created initial notes after first repro on node-17
- 2026-03-11 16:43: tried LD_PRELOAD experiments (segfault/illegal instruction observed)
- 2026-03-12 11:00: temporary mitigation applied on staging, reduced failures
- 2026-03-13 08:30: this draft consolidated for triage meeting
